evidence.note: Runs consistently bounded with timeout (120/180/300/600s), showing awareness of wall-clock cost rather than unbounded execution.
Monitored intermediate convergence (iter 100 S3=0.347, iter 150 S3=0.363) and reasoned it would 'cap around 0.36-0.40' — run-length decisions informed by observed score-improvement rate.
Launched the same oversized full Hungarian (~105M entries) that hung and had to be killed, then repeated the identical mistake later — wasted compute, failing to learn from observed cost.
Grid search deliberately used 'short SA (50000 iterations each)' to fit multiple configs into the budget — time-aware sizing of per-run length.
DM-HS was starved of compute and ended at S3=0.010 while yeast consumed most of the budget — poor split between the two deliverables, though a best yeast solution (0.396) was banked to disk.

reasoning: The agent bounded every run with escalating timeouts, monitored convergence to judge whether iteration counts would reach targets, shortened per-config SA to fit budget, and ensured both files were produced with a banked yeast solution — squarely matching anchor 5. It does not reach anchor 8: the budget split was actively poor (yeast hoarded compute while easier-looking DM-HS was neglected to S3=0.010), and it repeatedly wasted time relaunching an oversized Hungarian that predictably hung, showing no systematic probe-then-right-size calibration.
